p0000: EXHIBIT 10.2

p0001: SITE DEVELOPMENT AND HOSTING AGREEMENT

p0002: This SITE DEVELOPMENT AND HOSTING AGREEMENT (the "Agreement") dated as of August 9, 1999 is made between Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI"), a New Jersey Corporation, located at 1500 Harbor Boulevard, Weehawken, NJ 07087, and The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (the "Company"), a Nevada corporation, located at 2500 Arrowhead Drive, Carson City, NV 89706. Each of the parties hereto shall be referred to as a "Party".

p0003: In consideration of the mutual promises and covenants set forth below, HDI and the Company agree as follows:

p0004: 1. HDI's Responsibilities.

p0005: 1.1 HDI shall design, develop, implement, operate, maintain and manage, and enable the Company to establish a presence on the World Wide Web ("Site") to make available to Internet users on demand, men's and women's apparel and accessories from the Deerskin Catalog ("Deerskin Products"). As used in this Agreement, "Deerskin Products" shall not include (i) closeout merchandise which the Company may identify as "Deerskin" branded items, if such is the case, nor (ii) products from the Company's Joan Cook Catalog.

p0006: 1.2 HDI shall bear all costs associated with the design, development, implementation, operation, maintenance and management of the Site, including, without limitation, technology and labor.

p0007: 1.3 HDI shall host and maintain the Site on a server provided by HDI.

p0008: 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and

p0009: the right to use, a computer system on which the Site will be stored and operated, with a direct Internet connection of shared but greater than T-1 bandwidth, plus capacity to process continuously during burst periods. HDI shall also provide the Company with access to HDI's software and Content administration tools for purposes of allowing the Company to monitor current catalog information.

p0010: 1.5 For the purposes of collecting orders for Deerskin Products from the Site and to communicate to the Site the unavailability of certain Deerskin Products, HDI shall provide export files in the format provided by the Company. HDI shall bear the programming and software costs relating to efforts required to create order export files and receive and process import files of the Company's inventory information.

p0011: 1.6 HDI shall have the Site fully operational and accessible on demand by users of the Internet no later than sixty (60) days from the date this Agreement has been executed by both Parties. In the event that HDI fails to have the Site fully operational within seventy (70) days from the date of this Agreement, the Company shall have the right to terminate this Agreement without penalty.

p0012: 1.7 HDI shall distribute the Site through the world wide protocol of the Internet using distribution channels used by HDI sites and other similar distribution channels.

p0013: 1.8 HDI agrees that it shall promote the Site and Deerskin Products no less favorably than it promotes HDI's

p0014: catalog titles. HDI's promotion of the Site and Deerskin Products shall include, but not be limited to, the incorporation of the Site and Deerskin Products into HDI's promotion calendars with Xoom.com and Excite for the term of this Agreement. HDI agrees that the costs of any such promotions shall be borne by HDI.

p0015: 2. Company's Responsibilities.

p0016: 2.1 The Company shall provide all Content to HDI to be included in the Site no later than ten (10) days from the date this Agreement has been executed by both Parties.

p0017: 2.2 The Company shall bear all costs associated with the processing of customer orders.

p0018: 3. Fees; Payment.

p0019: 3.1 The Company shall pay HDI thirty percent (3016) of the Net Sales in excess of Eleven Thousand Dollars ($11,000) per calendar month. "Net Sales" shall mean all revenues from the sale of Deerskin Products on the Site including shipping and handling charges, minus refunds and exchanges.

p0020: 3.2 Payments to HDI shall be due monthly within thirty (30) days of the end of each calendar month and shall be accompanied by documentation reasonably detailing the calculation of the payment.

p0021: 3.3 Quarterly reconciliation of payments shall be conducted within thirty (30) days of the end of each calendar quarter to adjust for refunds and exchanges not taken into account in payments made to HDI.

p0022: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.

p0023: 4. Term; Termination; Termination Payment.

p0024: 4.1 Term; Termination. This Agreement shall be effective as of that date (the "Effective Date") the Site becomes fully operational as set forth in writing and executed by both Parties and shall continue for a period of one (1) year from the Effective Date. This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other. Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated (the "Termination Date").

p0025: 4.2 Termination Payment.

p0026: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.

p0027: (b) In the event that the amount of the Termination

p0028: Payment is determined pursuant to this Section 4.2 to be less than or equal to zero, then no Termination Payment shall be due to HDI nor shall HDI be required to make any termination payment to the Company if the amount is determined to be less than zero.

p0029: (c) The Termination Payment, if any, shall be payable by the Company in eight (8) equal payments to be made quarterly, commencing thirty (30) days after the termination date.

p0030: 5. Site; Site Management.

p0031: 5.1 URL. The Uniform Resource Locator, or address on the World Wide Web for the Site ("URL") shall be as mutually agreed by the Parties and shall be established and registered as necessary by HDI at no cost to the Company.

p0032: 5.2 The Company shall have exclusive artistic and editorial control over the Site, including, without limitation, the implementation of the Content on the Site and the design and look and feel of the Site. Neither the Site nor any portion of thereof shall be deemed accepted and approved by the Company unless and until the Company accepts and approves same in writing to HDI. No portion of the Site shall be made available on the Internet without the consent of the Company.

p0033: 5.3 The Company shall be deemed the "merchant of record" for all commercial transactions on the Site related to Deerskin Products. Until the sale of the Deerskin Products to the consumer from the Site all title to the Deerskin Products shall remain with the Company.

p0034: 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a

p0035: General Manager of its own to act as liaison with the other Party for the Site (each a "General Manager") who shall bear sole responsibility for bookkeeping and business operations of the Site on a day-today basis. Each General Manager shall have the authority to make and convey decisions on behalf of each Party and to be the liaison with the other Party for all production and Content matters.

p0036: 6. Exclusivity.

p0037: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.

p0038: The Company hereby grants to HDI a non-exclusive, limited, non-transferable license to use the Company's "Deerskin" trademarks, service

p0039: marks, and logos (collectively, "Marks") solely for the purpose of carrying out its obligations under this Agreement. Except as provided herein, no licenses of the Company's Marks are granted or implied under this Agreement.

p0040: 6.2 The Company retains the right to establish a web site on the Internet for the purpose of offering closeout

p0041: merchandise which may be identified as "Deerskin" branded products, if such is the case.

p0042: 6.3 During the term of this Agreement and for a period of two years after the expiration date of this Agreement, HDI shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet from which products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) are offered for sale to consumers on the Internet.

p0043: 7. Cross-Promotions.

p0044: 7.1 Joint Efforts. The Parties agree to cross-promote one another's products through the use of their respective customer e-mail lists on a reciprocal and equitable basis. The Parties specifically agree that the form, content and design of any and all advertisements or promotional materials featuring the other Party or such Party's products shall continue to be developed by or on behalf of such Party and shall be subject to such Party's final approval. The Parties agree further that any promotions or advertisements involving the use of a Party's customer e-mail list by the other Party shall be subject to the prior approval of such Party.

p0045: 7.2 Mutual Covenants as to Advertisements. The Parties hereby covenant and agree that their respective marketing and advertising efforts provided for herein shall at all times comply with all applicable laws rules and regulations and will

p0046: not contain any material which is obscene, threatening, fraudulent, harassing, libelous, infringing of third party intellectual property rights, otherwise illegal or, in the reasonable judgment of the Party required to display or transmit the advertisement, offensive.

p0047: 8. Confidentiality.

p0048: 8.1 Unless otherwise agreed to in writing by the Company, HDI shall maintain the strict confidentiality and shall not disclose to any third party the existence of, or terms and conditions of this Agreement. In addition, HDI, in performing the Services for the Company hereunder, may have access to or be exposed to, directly or indirectly, Content, user information, data, knowledge and proprietary and trade secret information of the Company in oral, graphic, written, electronic or machine readable form (hereinafter collectively referred to as "Confidential Information"). Confidential Information shall not include information which can be demonstrated:

p0049: (a) to have been rightfully in the possession of HDI from a source other than the Company prior to the time of disclosure of said information to HDI hereunder ("Time of Receipt");

p0050: (b) to have been in the public domain prior to the Time of Receipt;

p0051: (c) to have become part of the public domain after the Time of Receipt by a publication or by any other means except an unauthorized act or omission or breach of this Agreement on the part of HDI, its employees, or agents; or (d) to have been supplied to HDI after the Time of Receipt by a third party who is under no obligation to the

p0052: Company to maintain such information in confidence.

p0053: 8.2 HDI Obligations. All Confidential Information of the Company shall be held in strict confidence by HDI and shall not be disclosed or used without express written consent of the Company, except as may be required by law. HDI shall use reasonable measures and reasonable efforts to provide protection for Confidential Information, including measures at least as strict as those HDI uses to protect its own Confidential Information.

p0054: 8.3 Company's Obligations. The Company acknowledges that it may receive confidential information of HDI relating to its technical, marketing, product and/or business affairs. All such confidential information of HDI shall be-held in strict confidence by the Company and shall not be disclosed or used without express written consent of HDI, except as may be required by law. The Company shall use reasonable measures and reasonable efforts to provide protection for such confidential information of HDI, including measures at least as strict as those the Company uses to protect its own Confidential Information.

p0055: 9. Warranties.

p0056: (a) Each Party represents and warrants to the other Party that (1) it is a corporation organized, validly existing and in goodstanding under the laws of the state of its incorporation; (2) it has the full right power and authority to enter into, and to perform the obligations contemplated in this Agreement, and the person signing on its behalf has the full right,

p0057: power and authority to enter into this Agreement on behalf of the Party; (3) this Agreement constitutes a legal valid and binding obligation of the Party, enforceable in accordance with its terms; and (4) the execution of this Agreement will not conflict in any way with any pre-existing agreements or understandings of the Party with any person or entity.

p0058: (b) HDI acknowledges that the Company is currently a party to a web-hosting agreement with Globix Corporation (the "Globix Agreement") for the Company's web site offering Deerskin Products to Internet customers. HDI agrees that the Company shall not be deemed in breach of any provision of this Agreement by virtue of the Globix Agreement remaining in effect after this Agreement has been executed by both Parties, provided, that the Globix Agreement is terminated on or prior to the Effective Date

p0059: 10. General Provisions.

p0060: 10.1 Notices. Any notice under this Agreement will be in writing and delivered by personal delivery, express courier, confirmed facsimile, or certified or registered mail, return receipt requested and will be deemed given upon personal delivery, one (1) day after deposit with express courier, upon confirmation of receipt of facsimile or five (5),days after deposit in the mail. Notices will be sent to a Party at its address set forth above or such other address as that Party may specify in writing pursuant to this Section.

p0061: 10.2 No Joint Venture. The Parties agree that and acknowledge that the relationship of the Parties is in the nature of an independent contractor. This Agreement shall not be deemed to create a partnership or joint venture and neither Party is the other's agent, partner, employee or representative. Neither Party shall have any right, power or authority to enter into any agreement for or on behalf of, or to assume or create any obligation, liability, or responsibility on behalf of the other.

p0062: This Agreement will not be construed to create or imply an association, joint venture, co-ownership, or partnership between the Parties or to impose any partnership obligation or liability upon either Party.

p0063: 10.3 Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns, but no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement.

p0064: 10.4 Waiver of Breach. The failure of either Party at any time to enforce any of the provisions of this Agreement shall not be deemed or construed to be a waiver of any such provisions, or in any way to affect the right of any Party hereto to thereafter enforce each and every provision of this Agreement. No waiver of any breach of any provisions of this Agreement shall be effective unless set forth in writing and executed by the Party against which enforcement of such waiver is sought; and no waiver of any such breach shall be construed or deemed to be a waiver of any other or subsequent breach.

p0065: 10.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.

p0066: 10.6 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is declared invalid or otherwise determined to be unenforceable

p0067: for any reason, such provision shall be deemed to be severable from the remaining provisions of this Agreement, which shall otherwise remain in full force and effect.

p0068: 10.7 Survival. Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 of this Agreement shall survive and continue in full force and effect for a period of two years from the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

p0069: 10.7 Entire Agreement. This Agreement is the complete and exclusive agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, superseding any prior agreements and communications (both written and oral) regarding such subject matter. This Agreement may only be modified, or any rights under it waived, by a written document executed by both Parties.

p0070: 10.8 Headings; Counterparts. The section headings in this Agreement are for reference purposes only and shall not define, limit or affect the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement. This Agreement is being executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original but all of which shall constitute one and the same instrument.

p0071: IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have duly executed this Agreement as of the date first above written.

# Review: Site Development and Hosting Agreement — HDI (vendor) / Deerskin (customer)

**Bottom line:** The commercial deal (HDI builds, hosts and promotes at its cost for a revenue share) is attractive, but the risk allocation is unusually thin for a hosting/e-commerce agreement. The three things I would not sign as-is are (1) the Termination Payment formula, (2) the total absence of service levels, indemnities, IP/exit rights and any liability framework, and (3) the confidentiality/data provisions, which don't survive termination and don't restrain HDI's use of our customer data. Deerskin is also being asked to shut down its existing Globix hosting before it has any assurance the HDI site works.

---

## Priority 1 — Do not sign without changes

### 1. Termination Payment (§4.2) — effectively a perpetual lock-in

**Issue.** The payment is `(trailing 12-month Net Sales − $800,000) ÷ 2`. At $2M of Net Sales that is a $600,000 exit fee — roughly a full year of HDI's revenue share (30% of Net Sales over $11k/month ≈ $560k on the same numbers). Worse:
- It is triggered by *any* termination "by the Company," which under §4.1 includes ordinary non-renewal on 90 days' notice. Deerskin can therefore never exit without paying.
- It is not carved out for termination for HDI's material breach, insolvency, non-performance, or chronic downtime. We would pay HDI for HDI's failure.
- It is measured on **revenue**, not margin, and includes shipping/handling — it can exceed our gross profit on those sales.
- There is no reciprocal payment if HDI walks (HDI may terminate on 90 days' notice and owes nothing, leaving us with no site).

**Fix.**
- Limit to termination *for convenience by the Company during the initial term only*; expressly exclude (i) non-renewal at any anniversary on notice, (ii) termination for HDI breach/insolvency/SLA failure/§1.6 launch failure, (iii) termination following HDI change of control, and (iv) expiration.
- Convert the formula to a fee-based measure and cap it: e.g., "an amount equal to the fees payable under §3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date," or at minimum cap the current formula at a hard dollar number.
- State it is HDI's **sole and exclusive remedy** for early termination, is subject to Deerskin's right of set-off, and is non-accelerating.
- Confirm §1.6's "without penalty" language expressly overrides §4.2.

Suggested insert to §4.2(a): *"...provided that no Termination Payment shall be due if the Company terminates or elects not to renew (i) upon or effective as of any anniversary of the Effective Date, (ii) for HDI's material breach (uncured for 30 days), (iii) for HDI's failure to meet the service levels in Exhibit A, (iv) under Section 1.6, or (v) upon HDI's insolvency or change of control."*

### 2. No service levels, no remedies, no exit/transition rights

**Issue.** §§1.3–1.4 promise a server and "shared but greater than T-1 bandwidth" — no uptime commitment, no response/repair times, no peak-season capacity commitment, no backup/disaster recovery, no security obligations, no maintenance windows, no reporting. Our only stated remedy anywhere is the §1.6 launch-date termination right. Because HDI is paid on revenue share, downtime costs HDI 30 cents on the dollar and costs us the other 70 plus brand damage.

**Fix.** Add an SLA exhibit: ≥99.5% monthly availability (excluding scheduled windows), severity-based response/resolution times, nightly backups with defined RPO/RTO, capacity for peak (Q4) volumes, monthly performance reports, and a termination right (with no Termination Payment) for two SLA failures in any rolling six months. Add HDI responsibility for its subcontractors and prior notice of any platform/hosting migration.

### 3. Exit is catastrophic: no IP ownership, domain, data-portability or transition assistance

**Issue.** HDI builds and hosts the Site; the Agreement never says who owns the site design, code, configuration, or the **URL** (which §5.1 has HDI register). On termination we have no license, no code, no domain, no customer/order data export, and no transition assistance — and we may owe a six-figure Termination Payment. Meanwhile §9(b) requires us to terminate Globix, so we will have no fallback platform.

**Fix.** Add an IP/exit section:
- Deerskin owns all Content, the Marks, all Site customer and order data, and the domain name (registered in Deerskin's name; HDI to transfer/authorize transfer at our request and automatically on termination).
- Deerskin owns (or receives a perpetual, royalty-free license to) all Site-specific design, look-and-feel, HTML/creative and interface deliverables; HDI retains its pre-existing platform tools but grants a wind-down license.
- On expiration/termination for any reason: HDI provides up to 180 days' transition assistance at agreed rates, delivers all Deerskin data (including customer, order and abandoned-cart data) in a mutually usable format, and thereafter deletes/returns it and ceases all use of the Marks.

### 4. No indemnities, no warranties on the services, no liability framework

**Issue.** §9 contains only corporate-authority reps. There is no warranty that the services will be performed in a professional/workmanlike manner, no non-infringement warranty for HDI's platform, no malicious-code warranty, no compliance-with-law warranty. There are **no indemnities at all** and **no limitation of liability** — meaning unlimited exposure on both sides (including our exposure for an exclusivity or list-use dispute), with no consequential-damages waiver.

**Fix.**
- Add HDI warranties: professional and workmanlike performance; the Site/platform does not infringe third-party IP; no viruses/disabling code; compliance with applicable law (including payment-card and privacy requirements applicable to its systems).
- Add mutual indemnities: HDI indemnifies for third-party IP claims relating to the platform/technology, for security incidents on HDI-hosted systems, and for HDI's negligence/willful misconduct and misuse of Deerskin data or e-mail lists; Deerskin indemnifies for Content and product claims.
- Add a mutual cap (e.g., fees paid/payable in the prior 12 months) and a mutual consequential-damages waiver, with carve-outs for indemnities, confidentiality, IP infringement, data breach, and the Termination Payment.

### 5. Confidentiality does not survive; customer data is unprotected

**Issue.** §10.7 (Survival) lists §§6.3, 7, 9 and 10 — **Section 8 (Confidentiality) is omitted.** Read literally, all confidentiality obligations lapse on termination. Separately, §8 has no return/destruction obligation, no need-to-know limitation, no requirement to bind employees/subcontractors, no notice obligation before a compelled disclosure, no injunctive-relief acknowledgment, and no data-security standard beyond "reasonable measures."

Most importantly, nothing restricts HDI — a large multi-title cataloger with Xoom/Excite promotional relationships — from **using Site customer names, e-mails and purchase data for its own catalogs**. §8.1 nominally captures "user information" as Confidential Information, but confidentiality is not the same as a use restriction, and the 2-year survival cap in §10.7 would gut even that.

**Fix.**
- Add Section 8 to the survival list; make confidentiality survive 5 years (perpetually for trade secrets and customer data), notwithstanding the 2-year cap in §10.7.
- Add an express data clause: all Site user/customer/transaction data is Deerskin Confidential Information and Deerskin property; HDI may use it **solely** to perform under this Agreement; no use for HDI's own or any affiliate's or third party's marketing, list rental, appending, modeling or catalog mailings; no aggregation or de-identified reuse; return/deletion on termination; prompt notice of any unauthorized access.
- Add subcontractor flow-down, compelled-disclosure notice, and an equitable-relief clause.

---

## Priority 2 — Material, should be fixed

**6. Globix / Effective Date timing (§§4.1, 9(b), 1.6).** The Effective Date only occurs when both parties sign a writing confirming the Site is "fully operational" — HDI could withhold that signature indefinitely, and the interaction with §1.6's 60/70-day deadlines (which run from execution) is unclear. Yet we must terminate Globix "on or prior to the Effective Date."
*Fix:* Make the Agreement effective on execution, with a separate defined "Launch Date"; permit Deerskin to keep Globix live in parallel for 60 days post-Launch; condition the Globix termination covenant on the Site having operated in compliance with the SLA for 30 consecutive days; make §1.6's outside date a hard date with no Termination Payment and reimbursement of our reasonable transition costs.

**7. Net Sales / fee definition (§3.1).** "(3016)" is a typo; confirm 30%. The base is over-inclusive: it expressly includes **shipping and handling** (a pass-through to carriers) and does not deduct sales/use tax, discounts and promotional credits, credit-card fees, chargebacks and fraudulent orders, cancelled/undeliverable orders, bad debt, or gift-wrap. Also clarify that 30% applies only to the increment above $11,000 per month (and confirm the threshold does not roll over/aggregate).
*Fix:* Redraft Net Sales to exclude the above; state that refunds/exchanges/chargebacks are deducted in the month taken with a true-up, and that overpayments are credited or refunded within 30 days of quarterly reconciliation.

**8. Audit rights (§3.4) — HDI's own manager inspects our books.** Giving a competitor's General Manager access to Deerskin records is a competitive-information risk.
*Fix:* Audits by an independent CPA (not a competitor, bound by NDA, no contingent fee), once per 12 months, records limited to Net Sales calculation, during term + 12 months, HDI pays unless a shortfall >5% is found. Make the right reciprocal as to HDI's reporting/traffic records.

**9. Exclusivity scope (§6.1) is too broad and internally inconsistent.** "Any project similar to the Site... with respect to Deerskin Products **or products substantially similar** to Deerskin Products" could be read to bar Deerskin from third-party marketplaces, affiliate/portal programs, drop-ship arrangements with retailers, and even sales of comparable leather goods under other names. Also, the sentence grants HDI an "exclusive right to use the 'Deerskin' brand for a self-contained web site" while the next paragraph grants only a **non-exclusive** license — reconcile.
*Fix:* Narrow to "a dedicated, Deerskin-branded direct-to-consumer e-commerce web site offering Deerskin Products." Expressly carve out: closeouts (§6.2), Joan Cook, marketplaces/portals/affiliate and third-party retailer sites, wholesale customers' own sites, catalog/telephone/retail channels, informational or brand sites, and any brand acquired after the date hereof. Define "self-contained."

**10. Trademark license terms (§6.1) are incomplete.** No quality-control or approval right over HDI's use, no acknowledgment that Deerskin owns the Marks and all goodwill, no prohibition on HDI registering the Marks or Mark-containing domains/keywords, and no express termination of the license on termination with a short wind-down.
*Fix:* Add all of the above, plus immediate suspension rights for misuse and a covenant to assign any Mark-containing domain or registration to Deerskin.

**11. Assignment (§10.3) permits free assignment.** HDI could assign this Agreement — including our brand license, our customer data and the exclusivity — to a competitor (the clause even names Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled as competitors).
*Fix:* No assignment or delegation without the other party's prior written consent; narrow permitted-assignee exception excluding competitors; plus Deerskin termination right (no Termination Payment) on HDI change of control.

**12. Promotion commitment (§1.8) is unmeasurable.** "No less favorably than it promotes HDI's catalog titles" is unauditable, and the Xoom/Excite reference has no minimums.
*Fix:* Add a promotion schedule with minimum committed placements/impressions/e-mail inclusions per quarter, reporting, and a termination right without Termination Payment for material failure. This is our principal consideration for the revenue share — it should be enforceable.

**13. Merchant-of-record / order-processing cost allocation (§§2.2, 5.3).** We bear "all costs associated with the processing of customer orders" (undefined) and all merchant-of-record liability — chargebacks, fraud, consumer-protection compliance, and sales/use tax (note HDI's NJ servers may create nexus questions). Yet HDI controls the order-capture and data-transmission pipeline (§1.5) with no accountability for errors.
*Fix:* Define "processing costs" (limit to payment gateway/card fees, fulfillment, customer service); make HDI responsible for losses caused by its errors, mis-pricing, data loss or security failures in the order pipeline; allocate tax-determination responsibility and require HDI to support tax calculation/reporting; require HDI to maintain payment-data security and to notify us of incidents.

**14. E-mail list cross-promotion (§7.1).** "Reciprocal and equitable" is vague, and the clause contemplates a Party's *use of the other Party's* list — a privacy and list-asset risk.
*Fix:* No transfer of lists; each party sends on the other's behalf through its own or its ESP's systems; single-use only, no copying, retention, appending or downstream transfer; compliance with each party's posted privacy policy and applicable law; volume caps and mutual approval (already present); indemnity for misuse.

---

## Priority 3 — Missing standard provisions

Add: force majeure (with a right to terminate for extended outage, no Termination Payment); insurance (commercial general, professional/E&O, and — to the extent available — network security, with certificates); dispute resolution, exclusive venue (NY) and jury waiver; escalation between General Managers before suit; publicity/press-release consent (§8.1 covers confidentiality of terms but note HDI is an SEC filer — add a securities-disclosure carve-out with a request for confidential treatment, and be aware this document was filed as an exhibit); set-off; no third-party beneficiaries; change-control process for Site changes; records retention; compliance with applicable law (both parties); Content license grant to HDI (limited to the Site, during the term); acknowledgment that Deerskin's approvals under §5.2 do not relieve HDI of its performance obligations.

## Cleanup / drafting errors

- §3.1: "thirty percent (3016)" — numeral typo.
- Two sections numbered **10.7** and duplicate downstream numbering; §10.7 (Survival) omits §8 and also omits §§3 (payment true-ups), 4.2 (Termination Payment), and the exit/IP obligations we add.
- §10.7's blanket "two years" survival cap should be qualified ("except as otherwise expressly provided").
- §4.1: clarify whether the 90-day notice may be given at any time (termination for convenience) or only prior to an anniversary (non-renewal) — this drives §4.2 exposure.
- §1.6: 60-day launch deadline runs from execution, but our Content is due 10 days after execution — add a day-for-day extension only for our documented delay, with the outside date otherwise firm.
- §9(b): "provided, that the Globix Agreement is terminated on or prior to the Effective Date" — missing period; also see item 6.

---

### Negotiation posture

Items 1–5 are the walk-away set; they are conventional asks and I would expect HDI to accept most of them. Items 6, 7, 9 and 11 have real dollar value and should be traded together. Because HDI bears all build/hosting cost and earns only on a revenue share, HDI's strongest argument is that it needs the Termination Payment to recover its investment — the right answer is a declining, capped, initial-term-only fee with clean breach carve-outs, not a perpetual percentage-of-revenue exit toll.

# Review: Site Development and Hosting Agreement — HDI (vendor) / Deerskin (customer)

**Bottom line:** The commercial deal (HDI builds, hosts and promotes at its cost for a revenue share) is attractive, but the risk allocation is unusually thin for a hosting/e-commerce agreement. The three things I would not sign as-is are (1) the Termination Payment formula, (2) the total absence of service levels, indemnities, IP/exit rights and any liability framework, and (3) the confidentiality/data provisions, which don't survive termination and don't restrain HDI's use of our customer data. Deerskin is also being asked to shut down its existing Globix hosting before it has any assurance the HDI site works.

---

## Priority 1 — Do not sign without changes

### 1. Termination Payment (§4.2) — effectively a perpetual lock-in

**Issue.** The payment is `(trailing 12-month Net Sales − $800,000) ÷ 2`. At $2M of Net Sales that is a $600,000 exit fee — roughly a full year of HDI's revenue share (30% of Net Sales over $11k/month ≈ $560k on the same numbers). Worse:
- It is triggered by *any* termination "by the Company," which under §4.1 includes ordinary non-renewal on 90 days' notice. Deerskin can therefore never exit without paying.
- It is not carved out for termination for HDI's material breach, insolvency, non-performance, or chronic downtime. We would pay HDI for HDI's failure.
- It is measured on **revenue**, not margin, and includes shipping/handling — it can exceed our gross profit on those sales.
- There is no reciprocal payment if HDI walks (HDI may terminate on 90 days' notice and owes nothing, leaving us with no site).

**Fix.**
- Limit to termination *for convenience by the Company during the initial term only*; expressly exclude (i) non-renewal at any anniversary on notice, (ii) termination for HDI breach/insolvency/SLA failure/§1.6 launch failure, (iii) termination following HDI change of control, and (iv) expiration.
- Convert the formula to a fee-based measure and cap it: e.g., "an amount equal to the fees payable under §3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date," or at minimum cap the current formula at a hard dollar number.
- State it is HDI's **sole and exclusive remedy** for early termination, is subject to Deerskin's right of set-off, and is non-accelerating.
- Confirm §1.6's "without penalty" language expressly overrides §4.2.

Suggested insert to §4.2(a): *"...provided that no Termination Payment shall be due if the Company terminates or elects not to renew (i) upon or effective as of any anniversary of the Effective Date, (ii) for HDI's material breach (uncured for 30 days), (iii) for HDI's failure to meet the service levels in Exhibit A, (iv) under Section 1.6, or (v) upon HDI's insolvency or change of control."*

### 2. No service levels, no remedies, no exit/transition rights

**Issue.** §§1.3–1.4 promise a server and "shared but greater than T-1 bandwidth" — no uptime commitment, no response/repair times, no peak-season capacity commitment, no backup/disaster recovery, no security obligations, no maintenance windows, no reporting. Our only stated remedy anywhere is the §1.6 launch-date termination right. Because HDI is paid on revenue share, downtime costs HDI 30 cents on the dollar and costs us the other 70 plus brand damage.

**Fix.** Add an SLA exhibit: ≥99.5% monthly availability (excluding scheduled windows), severity-based response/resolution times, nightly backups with defined RPO/RTO, capacity for peak (Q4) volumes, monthly performance reports, and a termination right (with no Termination Payment) for two SLA failures in any rolling six months. Add HDI responsibility for its subcontractors and prior notice of any platform/hosting migration.

### 3. Exit is catastrophic: no IP ownership, domain, data-portability or transition assistance

**Issue.** HDI builds and hosts the Site; the Agreement never says who owns the site design, code, configuration, or the **URL** (which §5.1 has HDI register). On termination we have no license, no code, no domain, no customer/order data export, and no transition assistance — and we may owe a six-figure Termination Payment. Meanwhile §9(b) requires us to terminate Globix, so we will have no fallback platform.

**Fix.** Add an IP/exit section:
- Deerskin owns all Content, the Marks, all Site customer and order data, and the domain name (registered in Deerskin's name; HDI to transfer/authorize transfer at our request and automatically on termination).
- Deerskin owns (or receives a perpetual, royalty-free license to) all Site-specific design, look-and-feel, HTML/creative and interface deliverables; HDI retains its pre-existing platform tools but grants a wind-down license.
- On expiration/termination for any reason: HDI provides up to 180 days' transition assistance at agreed rates, delivers all Deerskin data (including customer, order and abandoned-cart data) in a mutually usable format, and thereafter deletes/returns it and ceases all use of the Marks.

### 4. No indemnities, no warranties on the services, no liability framework

**Issue.** §9 contains only corporate-authority reps. There is no warranty that the services will be performed in a professional/workmanlike manner, no non-infringement warranty for HDI's platform, no malicious-code warranty, no compliance-with-law warranty. There are **no indemnities at all** and **no limitation of liability** — meaning unlimited exposure on both sides (including our exposure for an exclusivity or list-use dispute), with no consequential-damages waiver.

**Fix.**
- Add HDI warranties: professional and workmanlike performance; the Site/platform does not infringe third-party IP; no viruses/disabling code; compliance with applicable law (including payment-card and privacy requirements applicable to its systems).
- Add mutual indemnities: HDI indemnifies for third-party IP claims relating to the platform/technology, for security incidents on HDI-hosted systems, and for HDI's negligence/willful misconduct and misuse of Deerskin data or e-mail lists; Deerskin indemnifies for Content and product claims.
- Add a mutual cap (e.g., fees paid/payable in the prior 12 months) and a mutual consequential-damages waiver, with carve-outs for indemnities, confidentiality, IP infringement, data breach, and the Termination Payment.

### 5. Confidentiality does not survive; customer data is unprotected

**Issue.** §10.7 (Survival) lists §§6.3, 7, 9 and 10 — **Section 8 (Confidentiality) is omitted.** Read literally, all confidentiality obligations lapse on termination. Separately, §8 has no return/destruction obligation, no need-to-know limitation, no requirement to bind employees/subcontractors, no notice obligation before a compelled disclosure, no injunctive-relief acknowledgment, and no data-security standard beyond "reasonable measures."

Most importantly, nothing restricts HDI — a large multi-title cataloger with Xoom/Excite promotional relationships — from **using Site customer names, e-mails and purchase data for its own catalogs**. §8.1 nominally captures "user information" as Confidential Information, but confidentiality is not the same as a use restriction, and the 2-year survival cap in §10.7 would gut even that.

**Fix.**
- Add Section 8 to the survival list; make confidentiality survive 5 years (perpetually for trade secrets and customer data), notwithstanding the 2-year cap in §10.7.
- Add an express data clause: all Site user/customer/transaction data is Deerskin Confidential Information and Deerskin property; HDI may use it **solely** to perform under this Agreement; no use for HDI's own or any affiliate's or third party's marketing, list rental, appending, modeling or catalog mailings; no aggregation or de-identified reuse; return/deletion on termination; prompt notice of any unauthorized access.
- Add subcontractor flow-down, compelled-disclosure notice, and an equitable-relief clause.

---

## Priority 2 — Material, should be fixed

**6. Globix / Effective Date timing (§§4.1, 9(b), 1.6).** The Effective Date only occurs when both parties sign a writing confirming the Site is "fully operational" — HDI could withhold that signature indefinitely, and the interaction with §1.6's 60/70-day deadlines (which run from execution) is unclear. Yet we must terminate Globix "on or prior to the Effective Date."
*Fix:* Make the Agreement effective on execution, with a separate defined "Launch Date"; permit Deerskin to keep Globix live in parallel for 60 days post-Launch; condition the Globix termination covenant on the Site having operated in compliance with the SLA for 30 consecutive days; make §1.6's outside date a hard date with no Termination Payment and reimbursement of our reasonable transition costs.

**7. Net Sales / fee definition (§3.1).** "(3016)" is a typo; confirm 30%. The base is over-inclusive: it expressly includes **shipping and handling** (a pass-through to carriers) and does not deduct sales/use tax, discounts and promotional credits, credit-card fees, chargebacks and fraudulent orders, cancelled/undeliverable orders, bad debt, or gift-wrap. Also clarify that 30% applies only to the increment above $11,000 per month (and confirm the threshold does not roll over/aggregate).
*Fix:* Redraft Net Sales to exclude the above; state that refunds/exchanges/chargebacks are deducted in the month taken with a true-up, and that overpayments are credited or refunded within 30 days of quarterly reconciliation.

**8. Audit rights (§3.4) — HDI's own manager inspects our books.** Giving a competitor's General Manager access to Deerskin records is a competitive-information risk.
*Fix:* Audits by an independent CPA (not a competitor, bound by NDA, no contingent fee), once per 12 months, records limited to Net Sales calculation, during term + 12 months, HDI pays unless a shortfall >5% is found. Make the right reciprocal as to HDI's reporting/traffic records.

**9. Exclusivity scope (§6.1) is too broad and internally inconsistent.** "Any project similar to the Site... with respect to Deerskin Products **or products substantially similar** to Deerskin Products" could be read to bar Deerskin from third-party marketplaces, affiliate/portal programs, drop-ship arrangements with retailers, and even sales of comparable leather goods under other names. Also, the sentence grants HDI an "exclusive right to use the 'Deerskin' brand for a self-contained web site" while the next paragraph grants only a **non-exclusive** license — reconcile.
*Fix:* Narrow to "a dedicated, Deerskin-branded direct-to-consumer e-commerce web site offering Deerskin Products." Expressly carve out: closeouts (§6.2), Joan Cook, marketplaces/portals/affiliate and third-party retailer sites, wholesale customers' own sites, catalog/telephone/retail channels, informational or brand sites, and any brand acquired after the date hereof. Define "self-contained."

**10. Trademark license terms (§6.1) are incomplete.** No quality-control or approval right over HDI's use, no acknowledgment that Deerskin owns the Marks and all goodwill, no prohibition on HDI registering the Marks or Mark-containing domains/keywords, and no express termination of the license on termination with a short wind-down.
*Fix:* Add all of the above, plus immediate suspension rights for misuse and a covenant to assign any Mark-containing domain or registration to Deerskin.

**11. Assignment (§10.3) permits free assignment.** HDI could assign this Agreement — including our brand license, our customer data and the exclusivity — to a competitor (the clause even names Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled as competitors).
*Fix:* No assignment or delegation without the other party's prior written consent; narrow permitted-assignee exception excluding competitors; plus Deerskin termination right (no Termination Payment) on HDI change of control.

**12. Promotion commitment (§1.8) is unmeasurable.** "No less favorably than it promotes HDI's catalog titles" is unauditable, and the Xoom/Excite reference has no minimums.
*Fix:* Add a promotion schedule with minimum committed placements/impressions/e-mail inclusions per quarter, reporting, and a termination right without Termination Payment for material failure. This is our principal consideration for the revenue share — it should be enforceable.

**13. Merchant-of-record / order-processing cost allocation (§§2.2, 5.3).** We bear "all costs associated with the processing of customer orders" (undefined) and all merchant-of-record liability — chargebacks, fraud, consumer-protection compliance, and sales/use tax (note HDI's NJ servers may create nexus questions). Yet HDI controls the order-capture and data-transmission pipeline (§1.5) with no accountability for errors.
*Fix:* Define "processing costs" (limit to payment gateway/card fees, fulfillment, customer service); make HDI responsible for losses caused by its errors, mis-pricing, data loss or security failures in the order pipeline; allocate tax-determination responsibility and require HDI to support tax calculation/reporting; require HDI to maintain payment-data security and to notify us of incidents.

**14. E-mail list cross-promotion (§7.1).** "Reciprocal and equitable" is vague, and the clause contemplates a Party's *use of the other Party's* list — a privacy and list-asset risk.
*Fix:* No transfer of lists; each party sends on the other's behalf through its own or its ESP's systems; single-use only, no copying, retention, appending or downstream transfer; compliance with each party's posted privacy policy and applicable law; volume caps and mutual approval (already present); indemnity for misuse.

---

## Priority 3 — Missing standard provisions

Add: force majeure (with a right to terminate for extended outage, no Termination Payment); insurance (commercial general, professional/E&O, and — to the extent available — network security, with certificates); dispute resolution, exclusive venue (NY) and jury waiver; escalation between General Managers before suit; publicity/press-release consent (§8.1 covers confidentiality of terms but note HDI is an SEC filer — add a securities-disclosure carve-out with a request for confidential treatment, and be aware this document was filed as an exhibit); set-off; no third-party beneficiaries; change-control process for Site changes; records retention; compliance with applicable law (both parties); Content license grant to HDI (limited to the Site, during the term); acknowledgment that Deerskin's approvals under §5.2 do not relieve HDI of its performance obligations.

## Cleanup / drafting errors

- §3.1: "thirty percent (3016)" — numeral typo.
- Two sections numbered **10.7** and duplicate downstream numbering; §10.7 (Survival) omits §8 and also omits §§3 (payment true-ups), 4.2 (Termination Payment), and the exit/IP obligations we add.
- §10.7's blanket "two years" survival cap should be qualified ("except as otherwise expressly provided").
- §4.1: clarify whether the 90-day notice may be given at any time (termination for convenience) or only prior to an anniversary (non-renewal) — this drives §4.2 exposure.
- §1.6: 60-day launch deadline runs from execution, but our Content is due 10 days after execution — add a day-for-day extension only for our documented delay, with the outside date otherwise firm.
- §9(b): "provided, that the Globix Agreement is terminated on or prior to the Effective Date" — missing period; also see item 6.

---

### Negotiation posture

Items 1–5 are the walk-away set; they are conventional asks and I would expect HDI to accept most of them. Items 6, 7, 9 and 11 have real dollar value and should be traded together. Because HDI bears all build/hosting cost and earns only on a revenue share, HDI's strongest argument is that it needs the Termination Payment to recover its investment — the right answer is a declining, capped, initial-term-only fee with clean breach carve-outs, not a perpetual percentage-of-revenue exit toll.
